Hi Sofia,

Appreciate the quick read — glad it moved so fast on your side. Answers inline below and I attached the completed spreadsheet plus two small artifacts you requested (SCIM sequence diagram + claim mapping samples).

1) OIDC session TTLs:
- Redwood supports configurable session TTLs at the tenant level for Dedicated and Private deployments. In Hosted mode we expose per-application idle and absolute TTL settings via the Console (Defaults: idle=30m, absolute=12h). For enterprise tenants we can extend those limits via configuration; policy-level controls can be tied to groups supplied by your IdP.
- Implementation note: session management is handled by our edge-auth proxy which honors ID token expiration and maintains a short-lived session cookie for downstream routing. Revocation: we support token revocation via an admin API (immediate) and a backfilled cache invalidation across nodes (under 60s typical).

2) SCIM semantics (PATCH vs full replace):
- Our SCIM implementation supports both PATCH (RFC 7644) for incremental updates and a bulk/replace path for customers that prefer full-state provisioning. For bulk operations we accept a single POST with a replace semantics flag; the endpoint performs an atomic swap for membership sets to avoid transient orphaned states.
- For very large deltas we recommend the two-step approach: POST with a staging namespace + swap operation (we implemented this pattern for a recent bank customer to reduce reconciliation windows). The attached scim_sync_sequence.png shows the staging + swap flow.

3) Admin delegation & RBAC:
- RBAC model: we expose role templates (admin, read-only-admin, group-manager, support-operator) that are configurable per tenant. Roles map to scoped permissions (route/model/console) and can be assigned to IdP groups via SCIM or linked via OIDC claims.
- Delegated admin and emergency escalation: Redwood ships a built-in emergency-access plugin that supports timeboxed elevation requests with an approver chain. By default it can be configured to require 1 or 2 approvers; it also emits audit events to the audit log and can optionally create a ticket in your ITSM system via webhook.
- Out-of-the-box workflows: for Hosted customers, we include the basic approval workflow; for Dedicated/Private customers we can enable the fuller workflow and integrate with ServiceNow/Jira for approvals.

Hi Sofia — quick answers from the infra side (I run the provisioning and runtime teams):

A) Sliding-window enforcement: yes — our edge-auth proxy enforces the idle TTL as a sliding window for all session activity, including API calls. We treat any authenticated request that touches the routing plane as session activity. For non-interactive jobs that authenticate with service principals, we recommend using long-lived service credentials with scoped permissions or short-lived access tokens with automated refresh (we can show patterns).

B) Staging flow recommendation for large deltas:
- Run the staging sync into a staging namespace (read-only for your production) and perform automated reconciliation metrics (counts, diff samples, membership tombstone checks).
- Once staging checks pass, call the atomic swap endpoint which performs a quiet replace of the membership sets. We batch the swap into smaller shard operations (by shard id) when delta > 500k to avoid long locks on the store.
- We also provide optional dry-run mode which will report the exact SQL-level ops expected for your sync so you can estimate lock durations.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute session to walk the SRE team through the diagram and run a dry-run against a small slice of your directory.
